title: Collective evolution learning model for vision-based collective motion with collision avoidance
short_title: Collective evolution learning for vision-based collective motion
abstract: Collective motion (CM) takes many forms in nature; schools of fish, flocks of birds, and swarms of locusts to name a few. Commonly, during CM the individuals of the group avoid collisions. These CM and collision avoidance (CA) behaviors are based on input from the environment such as smell, air pressure, and vision, all of which are processed by the individual and defined action. In this work, a novel vision-based CM with CA model (i.e., VCMCA) simulating the collective evolution learning process is proposed. In this setting, a learning agent obtains a visual signal about its environment, and throughout trial-and-error over multiple attempts, the individual learns to perform a local CM with CA which emerges into a global CM with CA dynamics. The proposed algorithm was evaluated in the case of locusts’ swarms, showing the evolution of these behaviors in a swarm from the learning process of the individual in the swarm. Thus, this work proposes a biologically-inspired learning process to obtain multi-agent multi-objective dynamics.

summary: Animal groups such as fish schools, bird flocks and locust swarms move together while avoiding collisions, guided by senses such as vision. We propose a vision-based model in which each agent learns, by trial and error over many attempts, to move with its neighbors and avoid collisions, so that group-wide collective motion emerges. We evaluated it on locust swarms, showing how these swarm behaviors can evolve from the learning of individuals.
key_findings: We propose VCMCA, a vision-based model of collective motion with collision avoidance that simulates a collective evolution learning process.
Each agent learns local collective motion with collision avoidance from visual input through trial and error over multiple attempts.
Locally learned behaviors give rise to global collective motion with collision avoidance across the group.
Evaluated on locust swarms, the model shows these behaviors evolving from the learning process of individuals.
